content:
Advertising will launch this summer on Apple Maps in the United States and Canada. Ahead of the official rollout, Apple has further revealed what is permitted and prohibited in Apple Maps ads.

Apple Maps advertising is about to arrive, and Apple has also disclosed the categories of ads that are prohibited.

Apple first announced plans to introduce advertising in Apple Maps back in March, saying at the time that ads would appear at the top of search results and in a new "Suggested Places" toolbar within the app.

Apple rolled out the underlying infrastructure with iOS 26.5 in May, including the new "Suggested Places" feature. But the company has not provided further updates on the official launch of Apple Maps ads since then.

According to TechCrunch, Apple has now updated its "Apple Advertising Services" policy to include new content related to Apple Maps.

The policy covers the overall advertising guidelines for Apple services including Apple News, Stocks and Maps, and lists detailed prohibited content that applies to ads across all services, including items such as violence, weapons and drugs.

Most notably, the policy further reveals specific restrictions for Apple Maps ads. Apple says there are three additional categories that are explicitly prohibited in Apple Maps advertising:

  • Home services: Ad content that includes or directly or indirectly promotes home services, including but not limited to plumbers, locksmiths, HVAC, pest control, roof repair or general contractor services.
  • Bail bonds: Ad content that includes or directly or indirectly promotes bail bond services or guarantee services involving pretrial criminal release.
  • Cryptocurrency ATMs: Ad content that includes or directly or indirectly promotes cryptocurrency ATMs.

In addition, Apple says ads involving medical services will be evaluated on a "case-by-case basis."

As TechCrunch points out, Apple's blanket ban on the entire "home services" category is worth noting. Home services is one of the major ad categories on Google Maps, but Apple clearly has no interest in them.

All indications suggest Apple is preparing to launch ads on Apple Maps imminently, but as of now there is still no official launch date.

The full list of prohibited ad categories is available on Apple's official website.
